name: Two-stage Ray Marching with Empty-Space Skipping
definition: A rendering optimization that splits ray traversal into two phases: Stage 1 performs cheap occupancy lookups to find the entry point into a volume, and Stage 2 performs expensive density sampling only after entry. This avoids evaluating complex density functions in empty space.
summary: Two-stage Ray Marching with Empty-Space Skipping accelerates volumetric rendering by using a flat occupancy map to skip empty space, distinct from hierarchical or distance-based methods.
